rows.nativeCandidateIfTheRuntimeGainsResource: GTFO-API LevelAPI.OnEnterLevel (`Invoked when Enter the level (Player is able to move)`, reached through EventAPI.OnExpeditionStarted and the native RundownManager.OnExpeditionGameplayStarted). The host's own GameBindings/LevelLifecycle.cs already subscribes to it, but the host exposes no package-visible equivalent: RuntimeLifecycleKind is Snapshot/StartupChanged/WorldChanged/TickAdvanced, and WorldChanged is raised by BeginWorld at level-generation start and level cleanup, not at `player can move`. A package would therefore have to subscribe itself, which needs `[BepInDependency("dev.gtfomodding.gtfo-api", ">=0.5.0")]` in ForgeMap/Native/Plugin.cs.

outcomeMapping.unknown: an end state outside the three publishes nothing and is reported once; it is never folded into one of the three

eventIdentity: forge.trigger.session.expedition_ended:<world epoch>:<end state>. The epoch makes an id unique across worlds (the kernel's replay ledger is per world), and the end state is part of the fact: the same end reported twice is the kernel's `duplicate`, while a different end state in the same world is its own event instead of an id conflict. Whether the game really reports more than one end for one expedition is an in-game check.
inGameVerificationPlan: Host, one level: the expedition ends and BepInEx/forge-logs/*.jsonl shows exactly one trigger.fired for forge.module.gtfo.map.binding.session.expedition_ended, followed by step.started/step.finished for a plan mounted on that level.

Outcome: clearing the expedition reports outcome succeeded, a wipe reports failed, and leaving for the lobby reports cancelled. Record which end states the game really sends for one expedition (one, or success then abort).
Client: a non-host runs the same callbacks and publishes nothing (no trigger.fired for this binding; the hook returns before the session).

Timing: the event still dispatches before the level is cleaned up — a plan's step must run, not merely be queued. If the game reports the end after OnLevelCleanup, the world epoch has already moved and the mount matches nothing, which is silence rather than a wrong dispatch.
Checkpoint reload: restarting from a checkpoint and then ending the expedition reports its own end once, and does not replay the previous world's event.
Two-level package: a plan mounted on level A is claimed when A ends and is not claimed when the package's level B ends (the mount comparison is the level identity, and the event carries no subject).
The blocked sibling: nothing fires for forge.trigger.session.expedition_started, because it is not registered; this row must be re-checked in game only after the runtime can carry its `map` port.

When the start row is implemented, its own four checks are: it fires exactly once per world at the moment the player can move (GTFO-API LevelAPI.OnEnterLevel, host only); a client publishes nothing; a checkpoint reload is recorded as either a new world with its own event or no event at all, whichever the game really does; and in a two-level package a plan mounted on level A is claimed in A and never claimed in B.
unproven: no game run: the hook was never installed in a live process, so call timing relative to OnLevelCleanup, the number of end reports per expedition and the client path are static conclusions only
